task_list: Replace drawQr() with a standards-compliant QR encoder that encodes setupData.provisioningUri, and add accessible text identifying the QR’s purpose.

Implement actual TOTP verification from the pending provisioning secret using HMAC-SHA1, six digits, and an appropriate accepted time window; ensure the mock code shown for testing is a code valid for that same secret.

Replace the hard-coded account-marcus-demo authentication behavior with a mock authenticated-user model that binds each authenticated identity to its own server-side account and rejects attempts to access another account’s MFA data.
Make MFA enrolment state account-level, deriving enrolled status from the authenticated account rather than initializing session.mfaEnabled to false on every login.
Require strict same-origin validation for all state-changing requests, including session creation, and implement an appropriate pre-login CSRF mechanism or equivalent same-origin login protection.

Add server-side failed-attempt tracking, rate limiting, and lockout for recovery-code verification; preserve or account-level-limit authenticator setup failures so restarting setup cannot bypass lockout.
Generate stronger recovery codes and store them with a salted, slow password hashing/KDF mechanism suitable for recovery credentials.

Remove the visible in-page credential log and stop logging provisioning secrets. Resolve the mock-console/security requirement conflict explicitly; if browser-console mock values must remain for assessment, restrict them to a clearly isolated test-only path and do not expose them in normal UI or production logging.

Replace email-only authentication with a server-side authenticated-user mechanism. Bind the MFA session only to a verified account identity; do not create/select an account merely because a user submitted an email address.

Ensure the simulated identity check is tied to the authenticated account owner’s approved mock delivery channel, rather than returning a usable identity-verification code to anyone who enters an email.

Add explicit browser console.log calls for the required test mocks: identity delivery code, authenticator provisioning/test verification value, and generated recovery codes. Keep these values out of server logs, URLs, storage, and error output.
Make the simulation testable with deterministic documented mock values, including a valid authenticator verification code or a deterministic test-secret/code mechanism that the server accepts.

Replace the custom QR implementation with a verified standards-compliant, self-contained QR implementation, or correct it by reserving all function modules before data placement, using correct alignment placement, and correctly implementing masking/error correction.

Validate provisioning-URI size before QR rendering and either choose a QR version/error-correction level that supports the payload or provide a clear manual-copy fallback without emitting a truncated QR code.

Fix account retrieval so sessionFor() resolves accounts by the immutable account ID stored in Session.accountId (for example, maintain a separate accountsById map while retaining an email lookup map for login).
Change /api/identity/request so it does not replace a currently locked identity challenge; return a clear 429 error until lockedUntil has passed.
Fix the recovery print handler by renaming the button variable and calling window.print().
Add accessible show/hide controls for the displayed authenticator setup secret and recovery codes, without persisting those secrets in browser storage.
Display a plain success notice after identity verification, using the server’s returned success message before or within the authenticator setup screen.

Make password verification timing uniform for existing and nonexistent accounts
  Add a fixed dummy password salt/verifier or perform a dummy passwordHash() operation when no account is found.
  Always perform one comparable password-hash operation before returning the generic authentication failure response.
  Preserve the same generic error message and status for invalid credentials.

Add strict server-side email validation to /api/authenticate
  Define a bounded email validation helper, including a reasonable maximum length and a conservative email format check.
  Normalize only after validating the input type and length.
  Treat malformed email values exactly like invalid credentials to avoid creating a validation-based enumeration oracle.

Implement a standards-compliant, scannable QR-code renderer for the otpauth:// provisioning URI using only code embedded in app.ts (for example, generated inline SVG or canvas data), and add it to the authenticator provisioning screen alongside the existing manual-secret/copy options.

Add an authenticated, CSRF-protected POST /api/recovery/verify endpoint that validates a submitted recovery code against account.recoveryVerifiers, rate-limits failed attempts, and removes the matched verifier after successful use so that each code is single-use.

Add a mobile-friendly recovery-code entry screen or reachable recovery verification flow with a formatted example, autocomplete support where applicable, clear error messages, retry support, and a plain confirmation after a recovery code is accepted.
Update the recovery-code UI wording only after task 2 is complete so that the statement “Each code works once” accurately reflects enforced server behavior.
